root_idea.summary: The root denotes departure from purity: uncleanness, dirt, or impurity, whether perceived by the senses or apprehended inwardly.
root_idea.development: Its semantic range develops from physical filth and impurity to moral or spiritual uncleanness, with related formations naming defilement, release from impurity, incurable disease, and apotropaic amulets.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The QAC-attested nominal form is the Quranic headword and merits its own public entry.

senses.definition: Spiritually or morally unclean; inwardly impure.
senses.usage_conditions: In the sole Quranic occurrence, this predicates uncleanness of those who associate partners with God. The usage concerns impurity apprehended by the mind rather than sensory dirt or physical contamination.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become physically unclean, dirty, filthy, or impure; physical uncleanness or impurity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sensory branch of the root, including verbal, nominal, and adjectival formations; it may be applied to a person or thing, including a garment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render a person or thing unclean, dirty, filthy, or impure; to defile.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative construction, including physical defilement and attested figurative or moral defilement. Form IV is cross-referenced with the Form II usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remove someone's uncleanness or impurity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported secondary usage of the same Form II verb, expressing the opposite result from the more usual causative sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To perform an act by which one becomes free from uncleanness, dirt, or impurity; to free oneself from sin or crime.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reflexive or middle construction describing an act that brings about freedom from impurity or wrongdoing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A specific ritual or legal impurity that invalidates prayer, such as urine, blood, or wine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional technical meaning in the language of religious law.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An incurable or treatment-defying disease; a malignant disease for which there is no remedy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions describing a disease or a person afflicted with such a disease.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An amulet, or the practice of hanging an unclean object, bones of the dead, or a menstruous rag on a person to ward off jinn or the evil eye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An apotropaic practice; the term may designate the hanging of the object, the object itself, or the related charming practice.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who hangs such objects or fortifies someone by charms or amulets.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An agent noun for the apotropaic practice associated with تنجيس.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small piece of skin placed on the notch or seat of a bow-string.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized material meaning distinct from the agent noun denoting an amulet practitioner.

cautions: The single QAC occurrence is the nominal form نَجَسٌ at 9:28:6. Lane records variant readings or forms around the Quranic expression, but those variants are not additional QAC form groups in this artifact.
